actor: API platform product manager at an ad-funded frontier-model vendor
job: Moving the newly priced mid-tier model API from public preview to general availability while holding its below-market anchor price.
outcome: A GA mid-tier API priced at or below the $1.25/M preview anchor, forcing rivals into a matching round toward sub-$1.
motivation: Ad revenue funds the model, so API margin is expendable; underpricing rivals buys share in the agentic-workload segment.

task.who: The vendor's model-API product and pricing team.
task.what: Ship general availability with aggressive mid-tier pricing.
task.where: The vendor's public developer platform and pricing page.
task.when: H2 2026, during the preview-to-GA transition window.
task.why: Anchor market price expectations below rivals' cost floor.
task.how: Preview usage telemetry and ads-subsidized margin modeling.

actor: Pricing strategist at a rival frontier-model vendor
job: Modeling competitive response to the $1.25/M anchor and drafting a sub-$1 price point for the vendor's mid-tier volume workhorse.
outcome: A published mid-tier price cut below $1 per million input tokens, with output pricing compressed proportionally.
motivation: The mid-tier is the price-elastic volume segment; losing it to a subsidized entrant erodes the whole API business.

task.who: The vendor's API pricing and go-to-market strategy team.
task.what: Draft and approve a sub-$1 mid-tier repricing.
task.where: Internal pricing reviews and the public API price list.
task.when: Late 2026 through Q2 2027, following Meta's GA round.
task.why: Defend share in the most price-elastic API segment.
task.how: Elasticity modeling of summarization and agent-pipeline demand.

actor: Inference-efficiency engineer at a frontier-model vendor
job: Cutting per-token serving cost of GPT-5.5-class mid-tier models via distillation, quantization, batching, and custom-silicon utilization.
outcome: A serving stack whose unit cost makes sub-$1/M input pricing gross-margin-positive rather than a loss leader.
motivation: Pricing can only follow cost; each serving-cost halving lets the pricing team match the war without burning cash.

task.who: The vendor's inference platform and model-optimization team.
task.where: The vendor's inference clusters and model-optimization pipeline.
task.when: Continuously through the runway to Q2 2027.
task.why: Make sub-$1 pricing sustainable at volume.
task.how: Distillation, quantization, speculative decoding, and hardware-utilization tuning.
